title: Baloch National Movement holds protest rally in Hannover against human rights abuses

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated against alleged human rights abuses by Pakistani forces in Balochistan, including enforced disappearances and killings.
tea.want: They demanded independent investigations into civilian deaths, accountability for perpetrators, and the right to self-determination.
tea.changed: Oct 12: The Baloch National Movement held a rally in Hannover, marching from Kröpcke to the Lower Saxony State Parliament.

summary: On October 12, 2026, the Baloch National Movement (BNM) organised a protest rally in Hannover, Germany, to highlight alleged human rights abuses in Balochistan. Participants marched from the central Kröpcke area to the Lower Saxony State Parliament, where they chanted slogans and distributed leaflets. The event featured addresses from BNM activists and representatives of the Pashtun Tahafuz Movement (PTM). Speakers raised concerns regarding enforced disappearances, arbitrary detentions, and civilian casualties, specifically citing reports of killings in the Panjgur district in August 2026. The demonstrators called upon the international community and the United Nations to conduct independent investigations into these incidents, including those involving military airstrikes and drone attacks. The organisers emphasised the need for accountability and the right of the Baloch people to determine their own political future.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The protest rally took place in Hannover, moving from the Kröpcke area to the Lower Saxony State Parliament.
